messages.subject: Question about nested logit model in mirt
messages.subject_clean: Question about nested logit model in mirt
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Chalmers,
I'm running the nested logit model in mirt for a project, and I have little questions I need your help with.
In the mirt package description (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mirt/mirt.pdf), page 176,  under the simdata function, itemtype says that "For nested logit models the ’correct’ category is always the lowest category (i.e., == 1)". So when we simulate response data using itemtype=nestlogit, the default is that the lowest category is zero and this category of zero is the correct answer (unless we define mins=1)
However, the example (p.180-181) says key=c(NA,NA,NA,1). I'm wondering if the key should be c(NA,NA,NA,0) because the item was simulated under the nested logit model using defaults.
When I ran the example code as it was (set.seed(201187)), the results are below:

$Item_4
          a1            d   g u  ak0  ak1      ak2  d0    d1      d2
par -0.903 -2.466 0 1   0 -0.477 -0.318  0 -2.622 -1.77

The discrimination parameter a1 is negative, which is odd because it is simulated from rlnorm(4,0,.2). I changed the key=c(NA,NA,NA,0) and the discrimination for the item simulated under the nested logit model is still negative. Changing the random seed did not help either.
So I'm wondering if I misunderstood something about the answer key and the negative discrimination. I'm using mirt 1.29. I tried the code in mirt 1.33.2 but the results stayed the same.
Thank you very much and I look forward to your reply.
Happy new year!!!
Best wishes,
Hoan Do.

messages.subject_clean: NA/Inf for SE while fitting Mutlilevel IRT models using mixedmirt
messages.body_plain:
Yes, the constraint means that a Wald test wouldn't be appropriate since by definition the parameters being tested against are exactly the same with the same variability. I think you want to use a score-test instead, as this is more about what would happen if a parameter was allowed to differ. You could also just do a likelihood-ratio test between the two models as you would have nested variants of each other, and for the most part the LR test is better than either the score or Wald when it is possible to fit both models. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Nominal response model output?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

That's an interesting question, as indeed the item category orderings according to the ak values do act much like one would see in the unidimensional nominal response model. THe resolution in this case is that the latent traits are assumed to be compensatory, and so are first collapsed to a single composite dimension within the NRM. Then, the ak values are interpreted as ordered given this weighted linear composite. In your thinking I assume that you want a model where the categories themselves are conditional on the latent trait of interest, in a way that is kind of like a non-compensatory model. I'm not aware of such a specification in the literature, but if you can reason out a reasonable probability function that would reflect this associated structure then I'd be happy to show you how it can be fit using mirt's more general custom item specifications. HTH, and sorry for the belated reply.

Phil

Phil

messages.subject_clean: Making plots for a multidimensional model without cross-loadings
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

For a project examining the properties of a questionnaire with 5 subscales I'm trying to fit a multidimensional model with a dimension/factor for each subscale. Because we expect items to only be related to the subscale they are a part of, we don't expect cross-loadings.

The resulting model looks something like this:
model <- 'F1 = 1-5
               F2 = 6-10
               F3 = 11-15
               F4 = 16-20
               F5 = 21-25
               COV = F2*F1
               COV = F3*F1
               COV = F3*F2
               COV = F4*F1
               COV = F4*F2
               COV = F4*F3
               COV = F5*F1
               COV = F5*F2
               COV = F5*F3
               COV = F5*F4'

Now, to get a better understanding of the item properties as well as test properties, I wanted to fit "Item Information Curves", "Item Characteristic Curves", and a "Test Information Function". However, when I do, I get the error message that mirt: "Can't plot high dimensional solutions".

I understand and don't mind this for the "Test Information Function" as I understand that it wouldn't make sense to examine these properties on the level of the multidimensional model, but more so on the level of the subscales (given that they are quite distinct processes such as commitment and exploration). As such, I think I can solve this issue by running the plot for the subscales separately.

However, I was wondering if there is a way of fitting "Item Information Curves" and "Item Characteristic Curves" for the full model? I think it shouldn't have to be a very complex plot, as for each item only one dimension/factor is loaded on. Is it possible to specify this, or should I create separate models for the subscales and then make the plots using these subscales?

I hope I have explained the issue enough and hope that someone can help me find the best way to approach this!

Thank you in advance,
Elisabeth de Moor

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I wondered how does MIRT guarantee that the signs of its loading ('a') estimates do not vary over different initial values? I tried to program a plain EM algorithm with optimx BFGS for nominal response models and to replicate the estimation results from the package, using the Bock1997 data. However, I noticed that, if my loading starting values are all positive, my algorithm would obtain loading estimates with all the signs reversed from those in the package. They are only correct if I use negative starting values. MIRT does not seem to have this issue, even when using random starting values that also seemed to be positive (code shown below). Is there certain constraint that needs to be built into the optimization to ensure the estimates always arrive at the correct signs from one starting values or another?

I dug around the documentation without much success. Did mirt determine the loading signs from data, or is it generally necessary to pick a certain starting value sign for these nominal models? Thanks for any input and suggestions!

Best,
Marco Chen

messages.subject: Plots for multidimensional models
messages.body_plain:
Hi mirt people,

I'm just going to start another thread because unfortunately the other one didn't get picked up.

For a project examining the properties of a questionnaire with 5 subscales I'm trying to fit a model with a dimension/factor for each subscale. Although some of these scales are somewhat related, we don’t really expect all scales to load on an underlying construct. However, for the purpose of parsimony we wanted to combine all subscales into one multidimensional model for the entire questionnaire. In this model, we expect items to only be related to the subscale they are a part of and thus, don't expect cross-loadings.

The resulting model would look something like this:

model <- 'F1 = 1-5
               F2 = 6-10
               F3 = 11-15
               F4 = 16-20
               F5 = 21-25

               COV = F2*F1
               COV = F3*F1
               COV = F3*F2
               COV = F4*F1
               COV = F4*F2
               COV = F4*F3
               COV = F5*F1
               COV = F5*F2
               COV = F5*F3
               COV = F5*F4'

Now, to get a better understanding of the item properties as well as test properties, I wanted to fit "Item Information Curves", "Item Characteristic Curves", and a "Test Information Function". However, when I do, I get the error message that mirt: "Can't plot high dimensional solutions".

I understand and don't mind this for the "Test Information Function" as I think that for this questionnaire (which doesn’t really have one underlying latent construct) it wouldn't make sense to examine test properties on the level of the multidimensional model. I think it would make more sense to examine “test” information on the level of the subscales (given that they are quite distinct processes). As such, I think I can solve this issue by running the plot for the subscales separately.

However, I was wondering if there is a way of fitting "Item Information Curves" and "Item Characteristic Curves" for the full model? I think it shouldn't have to be a very complex plot, as for each item only one subscale is loaded on. Is it possible to specify this, or should I create separate models for the subscales and then make the plots using these subscales?

I hope I have explained the issue enough and hope that someone can help me find the best way to approach this!

Many thanks in advance,
Elisabeth de Moor
